blocker.goal: Reach past riverside_hedge_meadow (240/0) right-exit hostile chokepoint to survey its unexplored east/south ground, identify the tile=0x50 objects, and find the A-slot item (sword) if it is there
blocker.location: 240/0, right exit chokepoint, on-screen stop position (44,12)
observations: 3 methodologically distinct approaches (raw Navigator.move! taps; Navigator.avoid_hostiles_and_push! default radius=16; avoid_hostiles_and_push! radius=32; avoid_hostiles_and_push! via a down-then-right alternate route) all converge on the EXACT same on-screen stop position (44,12) and the exact same HP floor (8/24 from a 24/24 start) -- technique-independent convergence, not a controller-skill gap.

2 OAM-confirmed tile=0x50 object pairs sit just past the chokepoint (screen x=70,y=30 and further east) -- static, non-mobile, 4-frame idle animation, never yet reached for a face+:a interaction test.

Room genuinely SCROLLS past this point (SCY shift observed, single tap moved y from 36 to 12) -- the chokepoint sits right around the scroll boundary, a plausible reason a fixed-radius avoidance primitive underperforms here specifically.
known_constraints: D12: no RAM writes to bypass the obstacle (0xDB5A must never be written)
no weapon/A-slot item confirmed owned yet
owner explicitly declined a D12 HP-write exception for this specific blocker and asked for a genuinely different approach instead

hypotheses.statement: The chokepoint is passable without any HP-floor regression below the already-established 8/24 by reading hostile OAM positions live each step and only advancing right when no hostile is within contact range (an opportunistic gap-dash), because the hostiles wander/patrol (documented elsewhere in this project) rather than permanently occupying the chokepoint -- a fixed-radius avoidance primitive (tested at radius 16 and 32) cannot exploit a moving gap the way a live polling loop can.

The chokepoint is a genuine structural gate: hostile patrol paths permanently overlap this exact screen position with no exploitable timing gap, so even an opportunistic gap-dash will still take unavoidable contact converging on the same (44,12)/8-24-HP signature already seen 3 times -- passing legitimately requires an item not yet found (a weapon or equivalent), not a better technique.

The 240/0 chokepoint damage is not purely from the wandering tile=0x6a/0x68 hostile: the 2 static tile=0x50 round objects near it (never contact-tested, closest approach only 25-30px) may be a variant of the oursin/sea-urchin hazard family already documented at riverside_flower_clearing (225/0, tile=0x5C/0x5E) -- a STATIC contact-damage hazard, not an active attacker. The signpost there explicitly says a shield protects against oursins specifically (dialogues.riverside_flower_clearing_sign, page 2: "Se proteger avec un bouclier!"), a claim never actually tested in-game (registry note: shield was only ever measured as partial knockback-mitigation against the WANDERING 0x60-family, never as a full block against a static oursin-type object). If true, deliberately walking into contact with a tile=0x50 object while shield-equipped (B held, facing it) should show ZERO HP cost on that specific contact, unlike contact with the wandering 0x6a/0x68 creature, which the D13 primitive already showed still costs HP even while shielded.

experiments.observation:
Checkpoint e240_confirmed (24/24 HP, x=20 y=36, room 240/0, shield equipped B-slot=4), 2 runs.
Run 1 (avoid_hostiles_and_move! bias toward :right): the hazard-avoidance dot-product picked
:up at step 3 (nearby 0x60-family wanderer), which -- per Navigator.move!'s own documented
boundary-rebase caveat -- silently crossed room_id 240/0->224/0 while still reporting :blocked;
9 further steps wandered in 224/0 (wrong room) burning HP 24->16 with the tile=0x50 object never
in OAM range. Discarded as a script artifact, not evidence either way.
Run 2 (plain Navigator.move_holding!(motherboard,:right,:b,min_hp:8) per step, room_id checked
every step to catch a repeat of run 1's silent room-exit): reproduced the established chokepoint
exactly -- stopped at (44,12), HP 24->8, still in 240/0, after 4 productive steps. OAM census
taken immediately BEFORE each damaging step cleanly attributes every HP loss to the wandering
hazard family, never to a tile=0x50 object: step2 (-1 HP, 24->23) nearest 0x60-wanderer at
28.2px (tile=0x50 present but at 43.9px, farther); step3 (-12 HP, 23->11) an under-tracked
tile=0x6c 'unknown hazard' sprite (Navigator::UNKNOWN_HAZARD_TILE_IDS, NOT in my wanderer query
until I checked it by hand) sat 5.7px from Link's pre-step position, no tile=0x50 object was even
on-screen at that moment (nearest_static: null); step4 (-3 HP, 11->8, the safety floor) a
tile=0x60 wanderer sat 2.8px away (essentially adjacent) while the nearest tile=0x50 object was
31.6px away -- matching, almost to the pixel, room_labels['240/0']'s already-recorded ~31px
closest-approach figure from the prior D13-primitive session. The static tile=0x50 object was
NEVER within Navigator::HAZARD_PROXIMITY_PX (16px) contact range in either run; closest live
reading was 31.6px, always with HP already at or crossing the 8-floor by the time the object
entered plausible range. Deliberate contact (walking INTO the object, facing it, shield held) was
therefore never attempted -- the HP floor was reached first, 3 productive right-pushes in, a 4th
technique-independent convergence on the exact same (44,12)/8-24 signature already seen 3 times
(raw taps, avoid_hostiles_and_push! r16, r32, down-then-right). Control comparison (not re-run,
from data/ram_registry.json's already-established Sept 16 2026 combat-contact test, 208/0): a
single stationary-approached 0x60-family wanderer took a full shield block (zero damage, 12-14
collision-seeking steps at 8.1px) in that room's less-dense setting; this run's denser,
multi-hazard 240/0 pocket (0x60 AND 0x6c both active near the chokepoint) showed only partial
mitigation -- real, non-zero damage on 3 of 4 productive steps despite the shield being held
continuously throughout (verified via Navigator.shield_equipped? and holding :b every internal
tap), consistent with this project's own established 'shield only partially mitigates in dense
multi-hazard scenarios, not a guaranteed full block' reading. GIFs:
data/recordings/2026-09-18_240_0_oursin_shield_test.gif (run 1, room-exit artifact),
data/recordings/2026-09-18_240_0_oursin_shield_test_v2.gif (run 2, the recorded attempt).
